pages.text: Vira Readiness Index — overview. The Vira Readiness Index is a per-parcel 0-to-100 composite score quantifying how viable a parcel is for new data center development. It is computed for every parcel in Prince William County, Virginia (159,181 parcels total) by spatial-joining the parcel against 30+ source layers, then combining 9 sub-scores using user-tunable weights. The default weights are: Power Readiness 20%, Regulatory Readiness 20%, Environmental Viability 15%, Water Sustainability 10%, Land Feasibility 10%, Time-to-Energization 10%, Political Risk 5%, Cooling Cost 5%, Development Cost 5%. Higher scores indicate better data-center-siting candidates. Hard-blocked parcels (federal land, state land, conservation easements, RPA, FEMA SFHA, wetlands) return scores in the 3-18 range and cannot be developed. The strongest candidates — M-2 zoning inside DCOZ with a substation under 1 mile away — score in the 80-100 range.

Power Readiness sub-score. Derived from distance to the nearest 230 kV-or-higher substation and the nearest 230 kV-or-higher transmission line, using the HIFLD Federal Electric Substations and Electric Power Transmission Lines datasets. A substation within 0.5 mi yields a Power Readiness score above 95; within 1 mi yields above 90; over 8 mi away drops the score below 35. Dual-feed capability (a 230 kV+ line within 0.25 mi in addition to a close substation) yields a +12-point bonus. The DC-corridor signal (5+ existing data-center buildings within 1 mi from PWC Data Center Buildings) adds another +6 points because nearby DC operators imply the grid is already built out to handle hyperscale load.

Regulatory Readiness sub-score. Combines zoning category, overlay-district membership, Special Use Permit (SUP) precedent density, BZA variance friction, MZP landbay designation, and inside-DC-campus flag. M-2 zoning (Light Industrial) is the canonical by-right data-center zone in PWC and adds +20. DCOZ overlay membership (Data Center Opportunity Zone, codified at PWC §32-509) allows by-right DC use and adds another +30. Outside the DCOZ, a SUP is required which adds ~12 months and ~20% historical denial risk. Residential zoning (R-2, R-4, SR-1, etc.) is treated as a substantial penalty (-25). A-1 agricultural zoning is moderately negative (-5) because rezoning is required. SUP precedent density of 6-30 historical Use Permits within 1 mi adds a small bonus indicating a familiar regulatory pathway. High BZA variance density (10+ within 1 mi) signals neighborhood resistance and subtracts 8 points.

DCOZ overlay (Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District) is the single most consequential regulatory layer for data center siting in Prince William County. Inside the DCOZ, codified at PWC Zoning Ordinance §32-509, data center facilities are permitted by-right — no SUP is required, no Planning Commission hearing, no community input period. Outside the DCOZ, the same parcel would require a Special Use Permit (SUP), adding 9-12 months to entitlement timeline, opening the project to community opposition, and creating roughly a 20% historical denial risk in PWC. DCOZ membership therefore raises Vira Readiness by +12 in the composite and +30 in the Regulatory Readiness sub-score. Of the 159,181 parcels in PWC, 1,831 sit inside the DCOZ. Hornbaker Road (GPIN 7596-81-5396) is the prominent live example of a parcel OUTSIDE the DCOZ that has applied for a SUP — this is why the parcel scores lower on Regulatory and why community opposition was documented at the September 24 2025 Planning Commission hearing.

Environmental Viability sub-score. Driven by hard-block overlays (RPA = Resource Protection Area under the Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act, ERPO = Environmental Resource Protection Overlay, Protected Open Space, Hydrological Features for wetlands), the FEMA SFHA flood zone, dam-break inundation hazard class (HIGH / SIGNIFICANT / LOW), and stream proximity. Centroid inside an RPA caps Environmental Viability at 22. Wetland centroid hit caps it at 12. FEMA SFHA caps at 8. ERPO is a softer overlay (Comp Plan watershed protection) that subtracts ~8 points but does not block development. Stream proximity within 100 ft triggers the RPA buffer setback and costs another 10 points. Dam-break inundation: HIGH hazard subtracts 20, SIGNIFICANT 10, LOW 4.

Water Sustainability sub-score and climate context. PWC is currently in severe hydrological drought. The latest NOAA Palmer Hydrological Drought Index (PHDI) reading for April 2026 is -5.30, indicating severe-to-extreme drought conditions. Vira's data-derived Water Sustainability baseline for 2026 is 48.8 out of 100, computed from PHDI as: 70 + (PHDI * 4). Under LOCA2 SSP3-7.0 (the IPCC AR6 baseline scenario), PWC's dry-day count is projected to hold roughly steady from 280/yr in the 2020s to 278/yr in the 2050s — the precipitation pattern shifts (more intense events, longer dry spells between) but total dry days are stable. Hydrologic soil group D (poor drainage) subtracts 6 points; HSG A (well-drained) adds 4. ERPO overlay subtracts an additional 4 because of stricter water-management requirements.

Cooling Cost sub-score and CDD trajectory. The LOCA2 SSP3-7.0 climate ensemble projects Prince William County's Cooling Degree Days will rise from 1,495 in the 2020s to 1,899 by the 2050s — a 27% increase. Vira's data-derived Cooling Cost baseline for 2026 is 80.2 (calibrated as 100 minus the CDD load above 1,000 base). Hot days at or above 90°F are projected to rise from 43/yr to 65/yr by mid-century. This drives the Cooling Cost sub-score's time decay rate of +13.44 CDD per year under SSP3-7.0, with the SSP scenario multiplier scaling decay: SSP2-4.5 = 0.6x (P10 / optimistic), SSP3-7.0 = 1.0x (P50 / baseline), SSP5-8.5 = 1.4x (P90 / pessimistic worst case).

Time-to-Energization sub-score and PJM interconnection context. The PJM Interconnection process for new generation or large-load interconnection requests is governed by PJM Manual 14H (New Service Request Cycle). The current cycle is 36-60 months end-to-end from initial study through commercial operation. PJM PlanningQueues data shows a Dominion-zone withdrawal rate of approximately 65% — meaning two-thirds of historical interconnection requests in the Vira coverage area have ultimately been withdrawn before energization. Vira's Time-to-Energization sub-score reflects this by: (a) crediting parcels inside an existing/planned DC campus polygon +10 (interconnection work likely already underway), (b) crediting M-2 zoning + DCOZ membership for fast entitlement, (c) penalizing parcels with 3+ Planning Pending Cases within 0.5 mi which signals queue + permit congestion.

Land Feasibility sub-score and construction inputs. Driven by acreage (parcels under 3 acres cap at 32; 100+ acres score 95+ baseline), soil construction category from the PWC Soils dataset (Category I = best buildability +5, Category IV = worst -6), slope percentage (15%+ subtracts 6 points, under 3% adds 1), LiDAR elevation range from the PWC Mass Points dataset (80+ ft variance subtracts 8 — significant grading required), easement intersection from the PWC Easements dataset (subtracts 4), and stormwater segment density (5+ segments crossing subtracts 4). Same-owner consolidation (the CAMA Parcel Ownership Table reveals when one entity owns 10+ adjacent parcels) adds 4 because site assembly is easier.

Political Risk sub-score and opposition signals. Combines BZA variance density (10+ cases within 1 mi = high friction, -12), pending case density (3+ within 0.5 mi = contested neighborhood, -4), building density at 500 ft (30+ neighbors = high opposition risk, -8), and DOCUMENTED OPPOSITION from PWC Planning Commission staff reports. The Hornbaker parcel (GPIN 7596-81-5396) is the demo-anchor live case: the Planning Commission staff report dated November 5, 2025 records 'four speakers, all in opposition' at the September 24 2025 hearing, citing concerns about electricity demand, water use for cooling, health impacts, the site's location outside the DCOZ, proximity to residential areas, and wildlife / migrating songbirds. This information was extracted automatically from the SUP2025-00016.json policy chunk via regex and is reflected in the parcel's opp_speakers = 4 and opp_topics_n = 8 attributes, lowering its Political Risk sub-score.

Development Cost sub-score. Combines acreage (>50 acres adds 8, <5 acres subtracts 10), hard blocks (RPA -18, SFHA forces score to 12, wetland -15), soil category (I = +4, IV = -8), slope (15%+ = -10, 8%+ = -4), easements (-3), LiDAR-derived elevation range (80+ ft = -12, 40+ ft = -5), land cover class at centroid (impervious = -5 because demolition required, barren / non-woody = +3 because already cleared, forest = -3 because clearing required), and dam-break inundation HIGH hazard (-8 reflecting harder permitting under VA-DCR rules).

Conviction score — data-depth meta-score. Separate from the Readiness Index. Conviction is a 0-100 score quantifying how many independent data layers contributed real signal for a specific parcel. Built additively from 26 distinct data inputs: CAMA owner record (8 pts), zoning (8), LRLU (6), DCOZ status (3), substation distance (6), transmission distance (6), SFHA (3), RPA (3), acres (3), soil category (5), watershed (3), wetland (3), ERPO (3), dam-break (3), DC-campus (4), MZP (4), SUP density (4), BZA density (3), DC-building density (3), easement (2), stream distance (3), land cover (3), stormwater segments (2), LiDAR coverage (3), policy mentions (3), active SUP (5). Plus a 10-point base for 'any parcel exists'. Conviction is the honesty layer: a 78 Readiness with Conviction 95 is meaningfully more trustworthy than a 85 Readiness with Conviction 40.

Quality flags on sub-scores: Measured / Modeled / Inferred. Each sub-score carries a visible quality badge. MEASURED (green border) means the score is computed directly from hard data — Power Readiness from HIFLD substation locations is Measured, for example. MODELED (amber) means the score is derived from inputs via an empirical model — Time-to-Energization is Modeled because it estimates a future outcome from PJM queue data + entitlement signals. INFERRED (gray) means the score is a low-confidence proxy — Political Risk is Inferred for parcels without documented opposition signals because we are estimating neighbor opposition from BZA variance density and building footprint density. When a parcel has documented opposition (like Hornbaker), Political Risk upgrades to Measured.

Timeline projection methodology. The Vira UI exposes a slider that projects Readiness forward from 2026 to 2050. Five sub-scores degrade over time under climate and grid trajectories: Power Readiness (PJM queue depth and transmission congestion grow), Water Sustainability (LOCA2 dry-days and PHDI worsening), Cooling Cost (CDD increases drive cooling load), Time-to-Energization (PJM queue density grows), Development Cost (climate adaptation premium). Four sub-scores are time-invariant under our model: Regulatory, Environmental, Land Feasibility, Political. The projection formula is: decayed_score = base_score * (1 - decay_rate * years_from_2026 * ssp_multiplier). SSP multipliers: SSP2-4.5 (moderate) x0.6, SSP3-7.0 (baseline) x1.0, SSP5-8.5 (high) x1.4. The cooling and water decay rates are derived directly from the LOCA2 ensemble trajectories: CDD slope of +13.44 per year, dry-days slope of -0.08 per year.

Data center market context for Prince William County. PWC currently hosts 51 approved or planned data center campus projects (PWC Data Center Projects dataset) and 203 existing data center buildings (PWC Data Center Buildings dataset). Approved cumulative gross floor area in PWC is approximately 122 million square feet; permitted GFA stands at roughly 23 million square feet. Major operator clusters are concentrated in Gainesville, Manassas, and Bristow magisterial districts. The DCOZ overlay maps closely to these existing concentrations. Vira's Data Center corridor signal — buildings within 1 mi of a candidate parcel — captures this market reality: a parcel with 5+ DC buildings within 1 mi receives a Power Readiness bonus because the underlying grid is provably built out for hyperscale load.

Policy corpus references. The Vira diligence engine indexes 22 Prince William County and Virginia policy documents in its RAG retrieval system: the 7-chapter 2040 Comprehensive Plan (Land Use, Environment, Community Design, Cultural Resources, Electrical Utility Service, Open Space, Technology / Connectivity), the PWC Community Energy and Sustainability Master Plan (CESMP, 199 pages), Resolution 20-773 (Climate Mitigation and Resiliency Goals), the Reference Manual for Rezoning / SUP / Proffer Amendment Applications, PWC Plan PP213 (Subdivision Regulations), the FY2026 SUP Application Package, PP-AddressValidationRequirements, PP-NewStructure-DataCenterBuildings, PWC Zoning Ordinance Chapter 32 excerpts (covering DCOZ §32-509, RPA §32-700, Airport Safety Overlay §32-505), JLARC's 2024 Data Centers in Virginia report (156 pages full + 34-page summary), PJM Manuals 14B (Transmission Planning), 14G (Generation Interconnection), 14H (New Service Request Cycle), the Virginia Clean Economy Act HB1526 (2020), and the SUP2025-00016 staff report for the Hornbaker case (the demo anchor).
